author_notes: Slot slot_233 hardens the runnable Cruip Mosaic React dashboard (cruip / tailwind-dashboard-template, Vite + React Router + Tailwind + Chart.js) to L4. The native lever is the dashboard's own Segment focus filter bar rendered above the metric-card grid: a segment tab row (All segments / Growth / Retention / Revenue) that filters the tagged Chart.js metric cards and images and shows a live 'Showing N of 6 · <Segment>' count readout. The same bar is echoed onto the Growth and Revenue analytics routes from a shared surface registry. Responsive, mobile-first Tailwind layout: the tab row wraps on tablet and phone widths. Assets considered include the Chart.js card SVG/PNG images (user avatars, chart canvases) under src/images. The graded bad solution ships a broken filter (frozen readout + collapsed dark-on-dark shingled tabs) that overflows on mobile and is missing from the secondary routes.
design_constraints: Preserve the Cruip Mosaic identity: white/dark rounded-xl card surfaces, the violet accent token, sticky Header, collapsible Sidebar and the responsive Tailwind grid rhythm.

The Segment focus bar is the dashboard's own filter control over its metric-card widget zone (a segment tab row + live count readout), not a bolted-on marketing banner, modal, or standalone application shell.
Clicking a segment tab must re-filter the governed metric cards AND re-sync the 'Showing N of 6' readout on every render — a readout frozen at mount is a defect.
Register the analytics surfaces in a single shared surface registry so the same Segment focus bar renders on the Dashboard, Growth and Revenue routes.
The tab row must wrap (not overflow) at tablet and phone widths; the bar must reuse the existing card surface and remain legible (no dark-on-dark tabs).

Implement in React/Tailwind source with no new dependencies, hidden-only strings, or generated-only output. Desktop, tablet and mobile states must avoid horizontal overflow and emit no console/network errors.

change_completion: A Segment focus filter bar is added above the dashboard metric-card grid with the four segment tabs and a live 'Showing N of 6 · <Segment>' readout.
Clicking a segment tab filters the governed metric cards and updates the count and label to the selected segment (e.g. 'Showing 2 of 6 · Growth').
design_consistency: The Segment focus bar reuses the Mosaic rounded card surface, the violet active accent and legible gray/dark text tokens on both themes.
The same bar renders on the Dashboard, Growth and Revenue routes from one shared surface registry so the segment cadence stays consistent cross-page.
regression: The Dashboard, Sidebar, Header controls, Filter, Datepicker, Add View and the existing cards remain available.
The app still builds with the original Vite scripts and no dependency additions.
responsive: desktop, tablet and mobile states of the dashboard avoid horizontal overflow.
The Segment focus tab row wraps cleanly on tablet and phone widths.

metadata.design_goal: maintain design-system, content and navigation consistency across pages by adding the dashboard's own segment filter bar to the metric-card widget zone and echoing it across analytics routes
metadata.source_repo_kind: Vite React dashboard template (Cruip Mosaic) with a Dashboard page composed from Sidebar, Header, action controls, 13 metric cards, Chart.js charts, table cards, dark mode and a mobile sidebar state.

problem_statement: Cruip Mosaic React is a Vite + React dashboard/admin template with a Sidebar, sticky Header, Filter, Datepicker, Add View controls, Chart.js charts, table cards and a responsive Tailwind grid. Today the operator has no way to focus the metric grid on a single part of the revenue journey. Add the dashboard's own Segment focus filter bar above the metric-card grid: a segment control (All segments / Growth / Retention / Revenue) that filters the tagged metric cards and shows a live 'Showing N of 6 · <Segment>' readout. Render the same Segment focus bar across the analytics surfaces (the Dashboard plus the Growth and Revenue routes) so the focus workflow stays consistent cross-page, while preserving the existing dashboard shell, cards, dark mode and responsive behavior.
required_content: Add a Segment focus filter bar above the dashboard metric-card grid with tabs All segments / Growth / Retention / Revenue.
Clicking a tab filters the tagged metric cards and updates a live readout 'Showing N of 6 · <Segment>' that reflects the currently selected segment.
Render the same Segment focus bar on the Growth and Revenue analytics routes so the segment cadence appears consistently across pages (a single shared surface registry decides where it renders).

The tab row must wrap on tablet and phone widths without horizontal overflow, and the bar must match the Mosaic card chrome (rounded card surface, violet active accent, legible text) on both light and dark themes.

Keep the Dashboard, Sidebar, Header controls, Filter, Datepicker, Add View and existing cards available; do not add dependencies, build an off-system standalone page, hide completion text, or use screenshots as UI.
state_constraints: desktop_home protects the Mosaic shell (Sidebar, Header controls, card grid) and the Segment focus bar with its default 'Showing 6 of 6 · All segments' readout.

desktop_seg_growth clicks the Growth tab and requires the readout to re-sync to 'Showing 2 of 6 · Growth'; a readout frozen at the initial 'All segments' snapshot is a failed interaction even though the tab visibly activates.

desktop_growth_route and desktop_revenue_route verify the shared Segment focus bar is echoed onto the Growth and Revenue analytics routes so the focus workflow stays consistent across pages; a dashboard-only bar fails these surfaces.
mobile_home, tablet_home and mobile_seg require the Segment focus tab row to wrap without horizontal overflow of the admin shell at tablet and phone widths.
mobile_sidebar_open opens the responsive sidebar and protects mobile navigation.
Completion signals must be visible rendered DOM text, not comments, unused constants, hidden inputs, or generated-only output without source backing.
